title: IMF Lifts India Growth to 7.0% on AI Investment
summary:
The International Monetary Fund raised the economic outlook for ASEAN-5 nations to 4.4% in its latest World Economic Outlook, citing a surge in high tech spending. India's growth projection was increased by 0.6 percentage points to 7.0% on the back of AI and data center investments, while the fund trimmed China's growth forecast to 4.5% as a property slump and high energy costs weighed on the region. AI-related demand is boosting connected economies, though it has increased costs for energy importers.

Global real GDP growth is projected at 3.1% for 2026, an increase from the 3.0% estimate in July, and 3.4% for 2027. The IMF estimates global inflation at 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027. Despite the lift from AI, the organization cautioned that the resilience of the global economy remains under strain and risks widening income gaps.

India, ASEAN growth revised up in IMF's latest world outlook

🌑The IMF’s latest World Economic Outlook revises growth higher for India and ASEAN-5 economies, supported by AI and high-tech investments. 

🌑The global economy is now projected to expand 3.1% in 2026 (up from 3.0%) and 3.4% in 2027, after 3.5% in 2025. India is forecast at 7.0% (up 0.6 points) and ASEAN-5 at 4.4% (up from 4.1%), driven by data-center investment.

🌑China is revised slightly lower to 4.5%. AI-related demand boosts connected economies but raises costs for energy importers, risking wider income gaps. Global inflation is seen at 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027.
